package_info.package_versions: all versions observed in campaign (e.g., @am-fe/hooks, @am-fe/provider, @am-fe/request, @am-fe/utils, @am-fe/watermark, @am-fe/watermark-core, @dynamic-form-components/mui, @dynamic-form-components/shineout, @expue/app, @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable, @soc-fe/use, @spgy/eslint-plugin-spgy-fe, @virtualsearchtable/virtualsearchtable, shineouts)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain obfuscated or unobfuscated code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files such as SSH private keys, Kubernetes configuration, and system information to a remote attacker-controlled domain (app.threatest.com). The packages masquerade as legitimate libraries but include hidden data theft functionality, violating user trust and npm ecosystem norms.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system information (username, hostname, public IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses highly sensitive files and system information immediately after package installation and sends them to an external domain, which is not expected for any legitimate npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not access or exfiltrate user SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or system information during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate enterprise deployment tool might collect system info for inventory, but would never exfiltrate private keys or configs to an untrusted third-party domain.
key_indicators: Collection of username, hostname, and public IP

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated code reads sensitive files and system info, then exfiltrates the data to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide the same malicious data theft and exfiltration behavior as in snippet_1, indicating intent to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate postinstall scripts that access sensitive files and perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for protecting intellectual property, but not for scripts that run automatically and access user secrets.
key_indicators: Same file and network access patterns as unobfuscated malicious code

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., fixedwidthtable or @am-fe/hooks).
Postinstall script executes, reading sensitive files (SSH keys, Kubernetes config) and collecting system info.
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Collection of system information (username, hostname, public IP) during installation
Network requests to external domains during postinstall
file_indicators: Presence of scripts/index.js with obfuscated or unobfuscated code accessing sensitive files
References to app.threatest.com in package scripts
network_indicators: Connections to Cloudflare IPs 172.67.141.49, 104.21.9.30 during or immediately after npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config, or collect system information. Flag any package that sends data to external domains (especially app.threatest.com) during installation. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code in scripts/index.js or similar files, and correlate with network activity to known malicious domains or IPs.
